correctness.rationale: Stationarity of the slow increment gives the exact mean \(\mathbb E[x]=\sigma-1\). Stationarity of \(y^2\) gives \(\operatorname{Cov}(x,y)=(\mu/2)\operatorname{Var}(x)\) with no use of the piecewise fast-map formula. Positive semidefiniteness of the covariance matrix yields the variance bound. Equality in Cauchy–Schwarz gives the affine slow–fast relation; combining it with the slow update at the image point forces reflection about \(x=\sigma-1\), hence period dividing two. The packaged checker verifies all moment and parameter algebra exactly.

value.rationale: The Rulkov model is built around a slow feedback variable driven by the fast membrane-potential coordinate, so the slow–fast covariance is a natural structural statistic rather than an arbitrary moment. The theorem shows that this covariance is not free: every compact stationary regime, from tonic spiking to chaotic bursting, has the same exact proportionality between covariance and fast variance. The determinant bound gives a parameter-scaled lower limit on slow-variable fluctuations, while equality has a sharp dynamical meaning—period at most two—so higher-period and chaotic regimes must lie strictly above it. This supplies a simple exact consistency test for simulated invariant statistics and separates minimal cycles from genuine bursting dynamics without relying on a local bifurcation approximation.
